text:
felix: quick heads-up: onboarding cust Avalon's LoRA merge (avalon-lora-0.9). Running the multilingual invoice evalpack and seeing locale-specific separator flips when using int4 quant. Spanish invoices switch dot/comma and lose cents. anyone seen locale swap issues after grafting localized tokens?

anika: that sounds like tokenizer+postproc mismatch. which tokenizer config did you merge?

felix: merge uses base multilingual v3 + graft: avalon-es-pretokens (adds currency and thousands tokens localized).

anika: paste one failing example? short snippet is fine.

felix: redacted sample below:

```
input: "Importe total: 1.234,50 EUR"
expected (postproc): "Total amount: 1.234,50 EUR"
model (fp16): "Total amount: 1.234,50 EUR"
model (int4): "Total amount: 1,234.5 EUR"  <-- US-style separators, cents truncated to .5
```

qa-bot: quick run: 150 samples (avalon invoice set), variants run: grafted+int4, grafted+int8, base-only+int4. Summary: grafted+int4: 21/150 locale-format errors; grafted+int8: 2/150; base-only+int4: 3/150. Latency int4 ~ -18% vs fp16. Artifacts: s3://redwood-eval/avalon/avalon-lora-0.9/1778889999/

anika: yikes. token dump for one bad case pls (tokenize + detok steps).

felix: token dump (grafted run):

```
# token ids (grafted multilingual)
[203, 4102, 9901, 700, 88, 3050, 11]
# detok before locale postproc:
"Total amount: 1 234 , 5 0 EUR"
# locale-postproc (es) -> "1.234,50 EUR"
# int4 runtime output -> "1,234.5 EUR"
```

anika: looks like the runtime is applying a different detokenization rule set (or a later stage uses en-US canonicalization). But weird that cents drop to single digit. Could be beam scoring prefers the shorter token for ", 5 0" -> ", 5" then postproc transforms to ".5" when interpreted as en-US.

felix: repro note: only when grafted localized tokens present + int4. Int8 & fp16 much better. Base-only still had a couple fails (likely model differences) but far fewer.

anika: two immediate checks: 1) force runtime locale=`es` via `--runtime-locale=es` to ensure postproc mapping uses Spanish rules; 2) enable `--debug-token-stream` in int4 path to capture model-decoded token sequence before postproc.

felix: kicked both off: `./evalpack --samples 150 --quant=int4 --runtime-locale=es --debug-token-stream`

qa-bot: debug run complete: locale pinned reduced locale-errors to 7/150. Debug token streams uploaded. Link: https://ci.internal.redwood/job/avalon/4521

anika: better but still wrong. Possible causes: 1) quantized logits causing preference for alternate tokenization that looks like en-US; 2) runtime inadvertently normalizing numeric spans to a canonical form before locale postproc due to a faster path in int4.

felix: any quick mitigation for the customer while we dig in? They need production stability.

anika: recommend short-term: pin Avalon to int8 for production canary. Also add a post-decode normalization guard that re-runs locale postproc with highest priority for numeric spans when locale mismatch detected. Longer-term: run a calibration sweep that includes grafted localized tokens so quantization preserves logit gaps for localized tokens.

infra-bot: scheduled canary pin: avalon-lora-0.9 -> int8 on stack-7 at 1778890020.

felix: opening ticket with token dumps, debug streams, and recommended rollout: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/ML-1372 (includes s3 artifact link).

anika: add a unit test to the graft merge pipeline: include a 30-sample multilingual invoice check with int4 and runtime-locale variations to catch regressions pre-canary. Also add a calibration target for localized tokens.

felix: will add tests and ping when CI green. thx all. :rocket:

qa-bot: artifact created: s3://redwood-eval/avalon/avalon-lora-0.9/1778889999/debug/ (token-streams, csv, evalpack logs).
